versionNote: 1.1.0 adds answerability.mjs, which navigates a running application and records what the recogniser made of each address, and framework-answer.mjs, which classifies an address against the configuration and is held against those navigations by --self-check. The comparison gained counts.missedPrefixRedirect and counts.missedPrefixUnanswered, and a lazy subtree read only in part is now reported as a failure rather than as a whole reading.
note: One entry per corpus application. `dist` is the built output, relative to the --dist-root the runner is given; `appDir` is the directory the extractor measured, relative to --corpus-root, and is where its uigraph.db sits. `adaptations` records every change the build needed that the checked-out source did not already carry, so a reader can tell what the probe ran against.
builtWith: Each application was built in its development configuration, because Angular removes the `window.ng` debug surface the probe reads when the application calls enableProdMode.

adaptations: angular.json names a global stylesheet inside a package the manifest does not depend on, so no install resolves it; the entry was emptied for the build. A stylesheet declares no route.
The runnable application is content-ce, which composes the measured library aca-content with the shell's own routes, so the framework's set is a superset of the measured directory's by construction.
The build emits one directory per locale under a base href, so the probe is served the whole tree and loads the English one.
The workspace declares only a production configuration, so the build ran with the bare options, which is what leaves the debug surface in place.
Built through the application's own webpack configuration with ENV=development.
